answers.answer: You do not have to create a bot account first. Once Twitch is connected, the bot can reply in your chat. Until a shared bot or your own bot account is connected, it types those replies from your own Twitch account, so you can test a command right away. When an account is connected, the bot uses the first connected one in this order: your own bot account (on White-label bot), then the shared bot, then your own Twitch account.
answers.quote: Until a shared bot or your own bot account is connected, it types those replies from your own Twitch account, so you can test a command straight away.

answers.answer: You must have connected Twitch first. The first paragraph says so and links to Connect platforms. Changing the Bot line marker needs the broadcaster role. Adding the shared bot needs the person who runs the installation.
answers.quote: After you connect Twitch, the bot can already reply in your chat.

answers.answer: Go to Settings, then White-label bot in the Bot group. The first row of the card Your channel's own bot tells you which account types the lines. The bot's name with a Connected badge and an @ handle means your own bot account. "Your channel uses the shared bot" followed by a login name means the shared bot. Shared bot with nothing after it means your own Twitch account. The Save step for the marker succeeds when the page shows "Basics saved." The marker test succeeds when the bot's !commands reply has the marker in front of it.
answers.quote: Your own bot account is connected, and the bot types from it.

answers.answer: Because a separate bot account is connected, the bot types from that account and leaves the marker off. The marker can still be saved but never shows. When that bot account loses the moderator role, the moderator notice checks it, and a notice titled "BotName is not a moderator in your channel" appears with the bot account's login name in place of BotName. It shows in Needs attention on the dashboard home and in the Action required list. The fix is to type /mod and that login name in your Twitch chat as the broadcaster and press Enter. The notice clears once Twitch reports the bot is a moderator again.
answers.quote: When either one is connected, the bot leaves the marker off.

answers.answer: The section on your own bot account mentions the marker and the moderator notice before either one is explained, so you read ahead or reread. It costs a moment of confusion, not a failed action. The status table's label Shared bot, when nothing follows it, means your own Twitch account, which you would not guess from the label. The table explains it, so it costs one reread.
answers.quote: When it is connected, the bot types from it, leaves the marker off its lines, and the moderator notice checks this account.
